summary: A separately stated delivery charge for goods that are exempt is not taxed in Missouri.

citations.title: 12 CSR 10-103.600(3)(A)2
citations.quote: If the purchaser is not required to pay the service charge as part of the sale price of tangible personal property, the amount paid for the service is not subject to tax if the charge for such service is separately stated.

citations.quote: Candy/snacks Taxable (reduced food tax rate)

citations.title: 12 CSR 10-110.990(1)
citations.quote: In general, qualified sales of food by a qualified business are taxed at a reduced state rate of 1.225% plus any applicable local tax.

notes: The reduced state rate is 1% under RSMo 144.014 plus the 0.225% constitutional conservation and parks/soils taxes, 1.225% in total (12 CSR 10-110.990(1)); the 4.225% general state rate applies otherwise. Candy has been SNAP-eligible food since before 1997; the DOR statements read are from 2023-2026. Missouri's SNAP restriction waiver (candy, soft drinks, energy drinks, pre-packaged desserts) was approved by USDA; DSS has reportedly moved its start from 2026-10-01 to 2027-02-15. RSMo 144.014 ties the reduced rate to items for which food stamps may be redeemed under 7 U.S.C. 2012; whether the waiver removes these items from the reduced rate is not addressed by any DOR source found. Review this rule before the waiver starts.

citations.title: Missouri DOR, Restaurants Tax Matrix (revision August 17, 2026)
citations.quote: Uniforms & shoes Taxable

notes: Date is the restaurant matrix's revision date; matrix expressly taxes uniforms and shoes, FAQ supplies the broad tangible-property rule. No permanent price exemption found. Back-to-school holiday temporarily exempts qualifying purchases from state and local tax; holiday is noted only. No differing general local clothing base stated on pages read.

summary: Packaged alcoholic beverages and drinks served at restaurants or bars are taxable at the general sales-tax rates.

citations.title: Missouri DOR, Restaurants Tax Matrix (revision August 17, 2026)
citations.quote: Sales of drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic) Taxable

notes: Date is matrix revision. General tangible-property taxation supports packaged retail alcohol; matrix explicitly confirms drinks sold by restaurants. Separate alcohol excises and municipal tourism/restaurant levies are not included. No differing general local sales-tax base stated on sources read; ordinary local sales taxes are included.
